editorial.headline: Paper Goods Wholesale: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale paper and cardboard goods—from bags and tissue to disposable diapers and sanitary pads—are nationally open to full foreign ownership, but PMA registration is blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
Wholesale paper and cardboard goods are the subject of this activity, best understood through its everyday inventory. It covers wholesale trade in paper bags, toilet tissue, disposable diapers and disposable sanitary pads: goods spanning packaging, hygiene and routine supply. Rather than treating those examples as exhaustive, the scope places them within a wider wholesale grouping of paper and cardboard goods. The classification therefore provides one commercial description for a varied but recognisably related set of products.

The activity is open at every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The record does not confine it to a narrow class of operator or to one point in a business’s development. A business undertaking this wholesale activity may register at any of those four scales, provided its commercial description remains anchored to the trade in the paper and cardboard goods within the stated scope. The breadth here comes from both the product grouping and the scale range.

At national level, the PMA position is unequivocally open. The maximum foreign ownership is 100%, meaning the national record places no foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. Its cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder reading the national position, the conclusion is direct: this wholesale activity is available for PMA registration nationally, across the stated scale range. That national opening is clear, but it is not the whole practical answer for a Bali-based registration.

Bali changes the result decisively. In Bali, the activity is marked Blocked (risk class) and is blocked for PMA registration. A foreigner cannot register it in Bali today. The operative reason is that, at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope. That brings it within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration in those risk classes, noted in May 2026 under Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. National openness does not override this Bali-specific block: the national and Bali outcomes for this activity are materially different.
